A0134.title: Address Obfuscation and Privacy Protocol Usage
A0134.definition: Avoiding address reuse and utilizing mixing services or privacy protocols (e.g., Tornado Cash, Zcash) to conceal transaction relationships.
A0134.description: On-chain transactions are publicly transparent, and address reuse leads to privacy leakage. Protection methods include: using a new address for each transaction (automatically derived by HD wallets); using privacy coins (Monero, Zcash) for sensitive transactions; breaking address linkage through mixing services (with compliance risks noted); adopting stealth address technology so that recipient addresses cannot be associated; and avoiding linking on-chain addresses to real-world identities (KYC platforms, social media). L2BEAT privacy best practices emphasize that address reuse is the greatest privacy risk.
A0134.limitation: Privacy protocols may be exploited for money laundering and face regulatory pressure; mixing services may exit-scam or be shut down by law enforcement; full anonymity impacts compliance and business applications; advances in chain analysis techniques may eventually compromise privacy protections.
keywords: Address Obfuscation and Privacy Protocol Usage

A0134-001.title: On-Chain Privacy Protection
A0134-001.description: Use mixing protocols, privacy coins, or zero-knowledge proofs to protect transaction privacy, breaking the link between on-chain addresses, real-world identities, and fund flows. Techniques include pooling multi-user funds through mixers and redistributing them, using privacy coins such as Monero/Zcash to conceal sender and amount, and employing zero-knowledge proofs to hide transaction details, thereby reducing the risk of on-chain activity being traced and attributed.
A0134-001.definition: Use mixing protocols, privacy coins or zero-knowledge proofs to protect transaction privacy.
A0134-001.limitation: Mixing services themselves may be exploited by attackers for money laundering, facing regulatory crackdowns (e.g., Tornado Cash sanctions) that render services unavailable or funds frozen; mixers carry the risk of exit scams; chain analysis firms can partially de-anonymize through transaction graph clustering, temporal correlation, and input-output amount matching, circumventing privacy protections; compliant exchanges may apply risk controls to addresses sourced from mixers, leading to legitimate users being mistakenly blocked and unable to withdraw assets after using mixing services.
